title: U.S. Space Force adds second surveillance sensor to Japanese constellation
summary: The U.S. Space Force has added a second surveillance sensor to Japan's QZS-7 navigation satellite, launched on August 10, completing a bilateral program to host U.S. sensors aboard Japanese navigation satellites.

title: Wallops gears up for an increase in launches
summary: Wallops Island is preparing for a significant increase in launches, prompting calls for infrastructure improvements to support companies and workers. This surge in activity highlights the need for upgrades to accommodate growing demand.

title: Spire and PlanetiQ win NOAA radio-occultation contracts
summary: NOAA awarded contracts to Spire Global and PlanetiQ for radio occultation data to support terrestrial and space weather forecasts. The contracts aim to enhance weather prediction capabilities using satellite-based observations.

title: Cheaper launch has moved the spacecraft bottleneck. Mass is out, surface area is in.
summary: The reduction in launch costs has shifted the primary constraint in spacecraft design from mass to surface area. This change reflects how advancements in launch capabilities have altered the challenges faced by spacecraft engineers.

title: Blue Origin outlines plans for second Cape Canaveral launch pad
summary: Blue Origin announced plans to expand its Florida launch site by adding a second pad for a larger version of New Glenn. The company aims to rebuild and enhance its Cape Canaveral facilities.

title: Intuitive Machines wins contract for three GEO satellites
summary: Intuitive Machines secured a $600 million contract to build three geostationary orbit communications satellites for an undisclosed customer. The deal was announced on August 13.

title: Bulgaria advances project to launch new space, defense innovation hub
summary: Bulgaria's government has approved a memorandum with EnduroSat to develop a new space and defense innovation hub. The project aims to advance Bulgaria's capabilities in the space and defense sectors.

title: In-Orbit Services Market to Generate $3 Billion in Revenue Over the Next Decade
summary: Novaspace's report projects that in-orbit services will generate $3 billion in revenue over the next decade. This highlights the early development and growing potential of emerging space services.

title: CesiumAstro buys semiconductor specialist to boost constellation plans
summary: CesiumAstro has acquired Jariet Technologies, a semiconductor specialist, to enhance its in-house capabilities for its phased-array antenna systems and future communications constellation plans.

title: Space Force awards five companies $60 million for multi-vendor satellite network tests
summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded five companies a total of $60 million to prototype and test connections to a data network backbone built by SpaceX. The companies involved are Amazon Leo, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Rocket Lab, and York Space.

title: 'Strap yourself in and feel the Gs': NASA announces 'Max Power' aerospace expo
summary: NASA announced a two-day aerospace expo named 'Max Power' scheduled for November. The event's name is a playful nod to 'Simpsons' fans.

title: Is empty space really empty? This magnetic star may finally solve a 90-year-old mystery
summary: A magnetic star, or magnetar, is being studied to potentially solve a 90-year-old mystery about the nature of empty space. Researchers suggest these astronomical objects can help test fundamental laws of nature.

title: Cards Against Humanity wants to erect a monument to 'honor' Elon Musk
summary: Cards Against Humanity announced plans to build a monument near SpaceX's Starbase site mocking Elon Musk. The satirical project is part of their ongoing public criticism of Musk and SpaceX.

title: 6 space board games to channel the political drama of 'For All Mankind' and 'Star City'
summary: An article lists six space-themed board games inspired by political dramas like 'For All Mankind' and 'Star City'. It highlights the theme of geopolitical competition in space.

title: Will the new moon race turn Earth's nearest neighbor into a dumping ground?
summary: Experts warn that the growing moon race could lead to lunar surface pollution if regulations aren't established to prevent companies from discarding old rockets on the moon. Rules are needed to protect Earth's nearest neighbor from becoming a dumping ground.

title: US Space Force gives Rocket Lab $397 million to build threat-tracking 'Flatellites'
summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded Rocket Lab a $397 million contract to develop 'Flatellites' for detecting and tracking airborne threats from space. These flat-panel satellites aim to enhance space-based surveillance capabilities.

title: Water can survive surprisingly close to the Milky Way's supermassive black hole, James Webb Space Telescope finds
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope discovered that water and cosmic dust can survive near the Milky Way's supermassive black hole, Sagittarius A*. This challenges previous assumptions about the harsh conditions in such extreme environments.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 14, 1992: Meteorite shower hits Uganda
summary: A meteorite shower struck Mbale, Uganda on August 14, 1992, after a space rock entered Earth's atmosphere and fragmented into hundreds of pieces.

title: ISS photobombs the sun during solar eclipse | Space photo of the day for Aug. 14, 2026
summary: The International Space Station (ISS) photobombed the sun during the total solar eclipse on Aug. 12, 2026, creating a striking space photo. This event was featured as the Space Photo of the Day on Aug. 14, 2026.

title: NASA Competition Invites Students to Help Imagine a Future Enabled by Lunar Technologies
summary: NASA has launched a student competition inviting U.S.-based collegiate teams to submit innovative concepts for lunar technologies in the 2027 RASC-AL challenge, aiming to envision future Moon operations. The competition encourages bold ideas to advance aerospace innovation and new technology paradigms.

title: NASA Announces MAX POWER: America’s Newest Aerospace Expo, Airshow
summary: NASA announced MAX POWER, a public aerospace expo celebrating American air and space innovation, to be held in Florida on November 7-8. The event will feature next-generation aircraft, spacecraft, and technologies.

title: Volunteer Develops Machine-Learning Tool to Identify Rare Clouds
summary: A volunteer developed a machine-learning tool to identify rare clouds that are appearing more frequently and lower in the sky. The NASA-supported Space Cloud Watch project encourages global participants to submit images of these clouds for scientific analysis.

title: NASA’s COFFIES Uses AI to Predict Storm-Causing Active Regions on Sun
summary: NASA’s COFFIES team has developed an AI model to predict active regions on the Sun that cause space weather storms. This advancement is crucial for future space exploration missions.

title: Total Solar Eclipse in Sunflower Field

summary: APOD features a total solar eclipse image from Greenland on August 14, 2026. The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) highlights a different cosmic phenomenon daily.

title: For West Virginia Engineer, Home Is Where the Heart Is… and NASA, Too
summary: A West Virginia engineer developed a passion for space exploration after a NASA field trip in 2013. The article highlights his early interest sparked by science fiction and NASA's Katherine Johnson IV&V facility.

title: Perseids Meteor Shower
summary: The Perseids meteor shower, one of the year's brightest, is active from early July through late August. The event is visible in the night sky, with a peak in mid-August.

summary: Blue Origin is nearing the end of its investigation into a catastrophic engine explosion. The company is also planning for a dual launch pad future.

summary: NASA has moved up the launch date for the Crew-13 mission to the ISS. The pilot of Crew-13 reflects on their career, training, and upcoming scientific objectives ahead of the flight.

summary: The first week of August is expected to be busy with multiple launches, including Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions. The launches highlight ongoing activity in the space industry.

title: TEC Business to Business website
summary: The news source is a B2B website focused on the technology, electronics, and computing sectors, covering business-related developments in these industries.

summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) released a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over its 50-year history. The publication celebrates key milestones and contributions to space exploration and science.

summary: Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona just hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission is part of ESA's technology demonstration program.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's precision in observing celestial phenomena.

summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by creating artificial eclipses and using computer models to simulate the event. This approach allows scientists to observe the Sun's corona for extended periods, aiding research that is otherwise limited by the rarity and brevity of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard ESA's Hera asteroid mission in deep space. This opportunity allows testing innovative software millions of kilometers from Earth.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical center in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to observe the Sun's corona by blocking the Sun's disk, simulating an eclipse. The mission involves two satellites playing hide-and-seek to achieve this.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands will bring together space startups and industry leaders to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaboration opportunities.

summary: Mantis Space has appointed Dale Parkes, a former Boeing executive, as its new Chief Technology Officer (CTO). The appointment coincides with the company's efforts to develop a constellation of spacecraft for continuous Earth orbit operations.

title: Telesat Remains Optimistic About Lightspeed Despite Shaky 1H26 Financial Results, Looming Debt
summary: Telesat remains optimistic about its Lightspeed satellite constellation despite reporting weak financial results for the first half of 2026 and facing concerns over upcoming debt obligations.

title: Optus Completes First Part of Project Aurora
summary: Optus, an Australian telco and satellite company, has completed the first phase of Project Aurora, a satellite life extension initiative. The milestone marks progress in extending the operational lifespan of satellites.

title: Marlink to Acquire U.K. Defense Comms Specialist GRC
summary: Marlink is acquiring U.K.-based defense communications specialist GRC to strengthen its position in European government, defense, and critical infrastructure markets. The acquisition aims to expand Marlink's capabilities in secure communications.

title: Space42 and Leonardo DRS to Boost UAE National Security
summary: Space42 and Leonardo DRS have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance national security in the UAE. The agreement involves Leonardo DRS providing its expertise and technology to support sovereign security initiatives.
